proof_scope: local deterministic Excalidraw toolkit validation, animation-token binding, create-svg scene compilation, create-svg SVG rendering, and fail-closed invalid board handling

claims.proves: the skill can validate its comprehensive reusable Excalidraw library (28 node blocks spanning generic strategy, system-design, memory, tau, and sparta vocabulary plus 5 animation tokens), compile a board with movable animation tokens into create-svg scene/timeline input, render that scene through create-svg, and reject an uncompileable board; it also validates vendored upstream v1-format libraries from the official excalidraw-libraries directory; the local whiteboard server serves the embedded page, lists libraries, renders a live board to SVG over HTTP, and fails closed on an invalid board; the served whiteboard page carries data-qid/data-qs-action/title instrumentation on its interactive controls; a mixed board with untagged vendored shapes compiles and renders; quickstart serves the whiteboard in one command; adversarial inputs (malformed JSON, unknown customData kinds, invalid accents, garbage HTTP payloads, path traversal) fail closed; an agent can hot-push a board to the running whiteboard over /board, the page polls and applies it, stale polls get 204, and invalid pushes get 422; the page and vendored UMD assets are served locally (no CDN) including query-string URLs; the page ships a dark/light theme toggle and opens the native library pane when a library is loaded; approved personal library items persist server-side to a versioned personal.excalidrawlib, are listed and reloadable, and invalid payloads get 422; the project agent controls the whiteboard entirely from the CLI: render-board compiles+renders a board to SVG (fail-closed on invalid), push-library persists custom items; sequential personal-library saves merge by id and never drop prior items (P0.5 fix); push-board defaults to a safe proposal (lands in /proposal, never /board; page shows Accept/Reject and merges by id so human elements are never deleted); --replace targets /board for a disposable canvas; describe drafts a fan-out board from a one-line spec (renders + pushes as proposal); a board with no animation tokens still renders (default reveal); the laser-pointer button is wired to Excalidraw's native setActiveTool; validate --profile fanout enforces the compiler contract (a passing validate guarantees compile, and it rejects exactly what compile rejects); the native-export button exports the board faithfully via Excalidraw exportToSvg with appState+files (preserves colors/images the semantic render drops); the local server refuses cross-origin browser POSTs (403), allows same-origin and CLI (no Origin), and caps oversized bodies (413)
claims.does_not_prove: every arbitrary Excalidraw layout, live browser editing, Excalimate compatibility, or final create-svg browser verification
